income_tax.note: No individual income tax of any kind.

senior_tax_credits.note: N/A -- no income tax to give a break against.

effective_rate_pct.unit: % of home value/year, statewide avg effective rate

new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.label: New buyer / recent purchase
new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.unit: % of purchase price/year, typical effective rate for a newly-purchased/non-homesteaded home before any Save Our Homes benefit accrues
new_buyer_effective_rate_pct.note: Save Our Homes resets assessed value to just (market) value at sale, so the statewide-average figure above (blended across homesteaded owners with years of capped assessed-value growth) understates what a new buyer pays in year one. Typical county millage is 15-25 mills (1.5%-2.5% of taxable value); e.g. Miami-Dade ~17.6 mills (1.76%), Broward ~19.8 mills (1.98%) for 2025. Not applied to the computed estimate below, which uses the statewide-average figure.

general_homestead_reduction_usd.unit: $ off assessed value, all homesteaded homeowners (approx.)
general_homestead_reduction_usd.note: Base $25,000 homestead exemption applies to all property taxes including school; an additional $25,000 (inflation-adjusted to $26,411 for 2026) applies to non-school taxes on assessed value between $50,000-$75,000 -- approximated here as a flat $50,000.

senior_homestead_reduction_usd.note: Additional low-income senior exemption exists but is county-optional and income-tested (see relief_programs_note) -- not applied here since it isn't universal.

property_tax.relief_programs_note: Save Our Homes (SOH) caps annual growth in assessed value at the lesser of 3% or CPI (2.9% for 2025) for homesteaded properties -- over time this can make the effective rate on a long-held home much lower than the statewide average, though it isn't modeled numerically here (this estimate uses the current market value each year). Additional senior (65+) low-income exemption: local-option (county/municipality must adopt it), requires household income at/below $38,686 (2025 AGI limit, applies to 2026), benefit $25,000-$50,000 additional exemption depending on home value and county -- not offered everywhere, not applied to the estimate below.
